source.document: Fluke 381 Remote Display True-rms Clamp Meter - Calibration Manual (Rev. 1, 06/2012)
source.pages: 11-12 and 14 (printed): Table 3 pp. 11-12 (PDF pages 19-20), Table 4 p. 14 (PDF 22); equipment Table 2 p. 8; Figures 3-7 pp. 8-10, 13-14; Specifications pp. 5-7
source.cite: Fluke 381 Calibration Manual, Table 3 Performance Tests and Table 4 iFlex Performance Tests, printed pp. 11-12 and 14; limits unchanged, rows flagged against the Specifications (printed pp. 5-7)
source.limits: Manufacturer limits, Tables 3 and 4, as printed (one set, no interval columns)
source.report_note: Limits are those of the manufacturer's Tables 3 and 4 (Fluke 381 Calibration Manual, printed pp. 11-12 and 14), unchanged. The current and frequency points are driven through a 50-turn coil (calibrator current x 50 = the reading shown), the 0 A dc point with a single wire, and the iFlex simulated points with a voltage on the iFlex input; the Uncertainty of a coil point is that of the 5500A/COIL scope lines at the effective current where they cover it, otherwise the calibrator's at the sourced current x 50.
source.note: Table 3 (40 rows: AC volts 7, DC volts 6, ohms 10, AC amps 6, DC amps 10, frequency 1; printed pp. 11-12) and Table 4 (7 rows: iFlex AC amps 6, iFlex frequency 1; printed p. 14) of the 381 Calibration Manual. The tables have no step numbers: steps are numbered in table order and the number runs on across the two tables (3-1 .. 3-40, then 4-41 .. 4-47 for Table 4 rows 1 to 7; the ref T4 #n of a point is the printed row). Table 2 (printed p. 8) names a calibrator with 4.5 digit resolution (Fluke 552xA), the 5500A/COIL (50 turns), the TP2 probe and test lead 6358; the program drives a Fluke 5522A, 5520A or 5560A (or you set the calibrator by hand). The AC / DC amps, frequency and iFlex-with-coil rows are driven through the 50-turn coil (calibrator current x 50 = the reading; limits are meter readings), the 0 A dc point with a single wire AUX HI to AUX LO (footnote [1]), and the two iFlex simulation rows with the calibrator VAC output (footnote [2]). The meter has no remote interface: you type the display reading. The manual prints one set of limits (no interval columns); they are used as printed. Where a printed limit is not the full accuracy of the Specifications (printed pp. 5-7) the point says so (five rows are the specification value rounded to the display step). The iFlex-with-coil tests (5 points) can be switched off before the run when the meter has no iFlex (the window option; the 2 simulation points always run). High-voltage points go straight to the test value (the manual prescribes no ramp). The functional checks and the calibration ADJUSTMENT (Table 5, printed pp. 15-18) are not part of this procedure.

381.name: Fluke 381
381.model_note: Fluke 381 remote display true-rms clamp meter (999.9 A jaw, 1000 V, 60 kohm, iFlex 2500 A): Tables 3 and 4, 47 points (42 without the iFlex-with-coil tests)

COIL_AUX.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator low-current output
COIL_AUX.summary: Calibrator low-current output (5522A / 5520A AUX HI / AUX LO; 5560A VI AUX / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the jaw ("Do not measure current while the test leads are in the input jacks", Safety Information, printed p. 2).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil

The wired coil is 50 turns (Table 2, printed p. 8: 5500A/COIL). Connect its two ends to the calibrator low-current output: Fluke 5522A / 5520A AUX HI and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A VI AUX (HI) and OUTPUT LO (Figure 4). Use plugs rated for the current.
Polarity

Polarity (Figure 4, printed p. 9, "Polarity is Reversed"): calibrator RED lead to the coil's BLACK terminal, calibrator BLACK lead to the coil's RED terminal, as drawn. For DC points a positive calibrator current must read positive on the meter.
Jaw
Close the jaw around the coil, fully closed, the coil centred in the opening, the coil leads kept away from the meter body. The meter then reads 50 x the calibrator current (0.2 A reads 10 A).
LCOMP

Fluke 5522A / 5520A: the program turns inductive-load compensation (LCOMP) ON for every AC point through the coil (read back with LCOMP?) and OFF afterwards (5522A Operators Manual p. 6-23; on the 5520A the command is UNVERIFIED). Where the calibrator does not allow it (440 Hz and above below 0.33 A; 1 kHz and above from 0.33 A) it is not set and the log says so. 5560A: no LCOMP command for its own output - set it yourself if needed.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_AUX.caution: This point drives current through a coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads. Do not measure ac/dc current in circuits above 600 V or 200 A with the jaw (Safety Information, p. 3).

COIL_20A.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator high-current output
COIL_20A.summary: Calibrator high-current output (5522A / 5520A 20 A / AUX LO; 5560A 30A / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the jaw ("Do not measure current while the test leads are in the input jacks", Safety Information, printed p. 2).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil
Move the two ends of the 50-turn coil to the calibrator high-current terminals: Fluke 5522A / 5520A 20 A and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A 30A and OUTPUT LO. The coil, plugs and leads must carry up to 19.5 A.
Polarity

Polarity (Figure 4, printed p. 9, "Polarity is Reversed"): calibrator RED lead to the coil's BLACK terminal, calibrator BLACK lead to the coil's RED terminal, as drawn. For DC points a positive calibrator current must read positive on the meter.
Jaw
The jaw stays closed around the coil (centred, fully closed, leads away from the meter body). The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 12 A reads 600 A, 18 A reads 900 A, 19.5 A reads 975 A.
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A / 5520A: AC points through the coil - the program turns LCOMP ON for each (and OFF afterwards), as for the low-current points.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_20A.caution: Up to 19.9 A flows in the coil. Duty (5500A/COIL data): 11 A rms continuous, 20 A rms for 2 minutes then 8 minutes OFF; not confirmed for this coil (UNVERIFIED). Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads.

WIRE_0A.title: Change the cables: single wire for the 0 A dc point (no coil)
WIRE_0A.summary: Calibrator AUX HI -> a single wire -> AUX LO (5522A / 5520A; 5560A VI AUX -> OUTPUT LO); the meter jaw closed around the wire.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the jaw ("Do not measure current while the test leads are in the input jacks", Safety Information, printed p. 2).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Wire
Table 3 footnote [1]: connect a SINGLE WIRE from the calibrator AUX HI to AUX LO (5560A: VI AUX to OUTPUT LO). Remove the 50-turn coil from the calibrator terminals for this point.
Jaw
Clamp the meter jaw around the wire only (Figure 3, printed p. 8). The calibrator outputs 0 A dc: the meter should read 0.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
WIRE_0A.caution: The calibrator output is 0 A, but the wire is a closed current loop on the calibrator terminals: keep the output in STANDBY while you connect the wire and keep clear of the terminals.

IFLEX_SIM.title: Change the cables: iFlex simulation (calibrator voltage output to the iFlex input)
IFLEX_SIM.summary: Calibrator NORMAL HI (5522A / 5520A) / OUTPUT V/Ω HI (5560A) -> iFlex 2 mm jack (far left); calibrator LO -> the black COM jack. Test lead with retractable sheath (6358, PN 1903307) and 2 mm to 4 mm Slim Reach probe (TP2, PN 650892).
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Calibrator
Fluke 5522A / 5520A: NORMAL HI and NORMAL LO; Fluke 5560A: OUTPUT V/Ω HI and OUTPUT V/Ω LO (the voltage output, as for the volts points).
iFlex input

Calibrator HI to the iFlex 2 mm jack on the far left of the meter, calibrator LO to the black COM jack (iFlex paragraph, printed p. 13; Figure 7, printed p. 14). Use the test probe for iFlex (2 mm to 4 mm Slim Reach probe, TP2, PN 650892) and the test lead with retractable sheath (6358, PN 1903307). No iFlex loop is connected. The far-left small jack in Figure 1 (unlabelled in the manual) is the iFlex input (owner-confirmed).
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
IFLEX_SIM.caution: The output is only millivolts (75 and 750 mV). Keep the calibrator in STANDBY while you connect the leads.

IFLEX_COIL_AUX.title: Change the cables: iFlex loop on the 50-turn coil, calibrator low-current output
IFLEX_COIL_AUX.summary: Calibrator low-current output (5522A / 5520A AUX HI / AUX LO; 5560A VI AUX / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the iFlex loop around the coil, plugged into the meter. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the iFlex ("Do not measure current while the test leads are in the input jacks", Safety Information, printed p. 2).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil
Coil on the calibrator low-current output as for the jaw points: Fluke 5522A / 5520A AUX HI and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A VI AUX (HI) and OUTPUT LO.
iFlex

Remove the jaw from the coil. Plug the iFlex probe into the meter and place its loop around the coil (Table 4 footnote [1], Figure 6, printed p. 13). The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 0.2 A reads 10 A. The iFlex error is 0.5 % / 1.0 % / 2.0 % by the distance of the conductor from the optimum position (Figure 2, printed p. 6): centre the coil in the loop. How the loop sits on the 5500A/COIL is not described: UNVERIFIED.
LCOMP

Fluke 5522A / 5520A: the program turns inductive-load compensation (LCOMP) ON for every AC point through the coil (read back with LCOMP?) and OFF afterwards (5522A Operators Manual p. 6-23; on the 5520A the command is UNVERIFIED). Where the calibrator does not allow it (440 Hz and above below 0.33 A; 1 kHz and above from 0.33 A) it is not set and the log says so. 5560A: no LCOMP command for its own output - set it yourself if needed.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
IFLEX_COIL_AUX.caution: This point drives current through a coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil, the loop or the leads. Do not apply the iFlex around or remove it from hazardous live conductors (Safety Information, p. 3).

IFLEX_COIL_20A.title: Change the cables: iFlex loop on the 50-turn coil, calibrator high-current output
IFLEX_COIL_20A.summary: Calibrator high-current output (5522A / 5520A 20 A / AUX LO; 5560A 30A / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the iFlex loop around the coil, plugged into the meter. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the iFlex ("Do not measure current while the test leads are in the input jacks", Safety Information, printed p. 2).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil
Move the two ends of the coil to the calibrator high-current terminals: Fluke 5522A / 5520A 20 A and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A 30A and OUTPUT LO. The coil, plugs and leads must carry up to 19.9 A.
iFlex
The iFlex loop stays around the coil, the probe plugged into the meter. The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 12 A reads 600 A, 19.9 A reads 995 A.
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A / 5520A: AC points through the coil - the program turns LCOMP ON for each (and OFF afterwards).
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
IFLEX_COIL_20A.caution: Up to 19.9 A flows in the coil. Duty (5500A/COIL data): 11 A rms continuous, 20 A rms for 2 minutes then 8 minutes OFF; not confirmed for this coil (UNVERIFIED). Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads.

steps.note: Tables 3 / 4 name no range: the range shown is the one the published resolutions put this reading in (Specifications, printed pp. 5-7; the meter autoranges). iFlex simulation (Table 4 footnote [2], Figure 7, printed p. 14): calibrator VAC output HI to the iFlex 2 mm jack (far left; the small far-left jack is the iFlex input, owner-confirmed), LO to the black COM jack; the calibrator drives 750 mV AC at 500 Hz and the meter reads 2500 A (the simulated coil voltage is proportional to frequency: 30 uV per A at 50 Hz, 300 uV per A at 500 Hz). Uncertainty (the 376 convention): the regular calibrator AC VOLTS uncertainty at the output as printed; TAR / TUR stay blank (the tolerance is in amps, the uncertainty in volts). iFlex range 999.9 A / 2500 A: 0.1 A resolution up to 999.9 A, 1 A above (Specifications, printed p. 5).

steps.dsb_desc: Frequency, iFlex loop on the 50-turn coil: calibrator 0.4 A @ 50 Hz, meter reads 50 Hz
steps.note: Tables 3 / 4 name no range: the range shown is the one the published resolutions put this reading in (Specifications, printed pp. 5-7; the meter autoranges). The calibrator drives 0.4 A at 50 Hz through the 50-turn coil (20.0 A in the iFlex loop) and the meter shows the FREQUENCY. The test current is exactly the trigger level in the Specifications (iFlex 20 to 100 Hz: 20 A or more); a marginal trigger may need the point repeated (UNVERIFIED). Uncertainty (owner decision, 2026-10-26, all handheld meters): the frequency is the calibrator's own OUTPUT frequency, so the uncertainty is the calibrator's published frequency specification (5522A / 5520A sheet or 5560A sheet, uncertainty_budget FREQ), not the lab Frequency - Measure CMC alone. CHECK (printed limit not changed; Calibration Manual Specifications pp. 6-7): the printed limit is the specification value rounded to the display step (high limit ±0.8 from the nominal vs the published ±0.75).
